chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-ʿAlawī, from Sahl ibn Jumhūr, from ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥasanī, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥusayn al-ʿUranī, from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
“Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام forbade that a man perform tayammum with dust from the trace of the road.”

These two reports indicate the reprehensibility of tayammum from the trace of the road and trodden places, so after this there remains only elevated grounds and high places from which tayammum is recommended.

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: tayammum is not permissible with anything other than earth from what the earth grows, even if it resembles dust in its softness and fineness, such as ushnān, suʿd, sidr, and the like. Tayammum with ashes is not permissible, and there is no harm in performing tayammum with white gypsum earth and nūrah earth.

When it has been established by what we have mentioned that tayammum must be with dust, earth, or that to which the name of dust or earth applies unqualifiedly, and these things are among what the name of dust or earth does not apply to, then it follows that tayammum with them is not permissible; and this is also indicated by further evidence.

key_terms.أَثَرِ الطَّرِيقِ: the trace of the road, meaning roadway dust or soil from commonly traveled paths
key_terms.التَّيَمُّمُ: dry ablution performed in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath) under specific conditions
key_terms.التُّرَابِ: dust or soil used as a valid material for tayammum
key_terms.الرَّمَادِ: ashes, explicitly stated here as invalid for tayammum
key_terms.النُّورَةِ: nūrah earth, a calcareous or lime-like earth deemed permissible here
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: earth or ground, the foundational valid medium for tayammum
key_terms.الْجِصِّيَّةِ: gypsum-like earth, mentioned as permissible for tayammum
key_terms.الْمَوَاضِعِ الْمُوطَّأَةِ: trodden places, areas repeatedly stepped on

ai.seo_question: What materials are permissible and impermissible for tayammum in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal rules of tayammum, stating that it is disliked to perform it with dust from roadways and heavily trodden places. It further clarifies that tayammum is only valid with earth or substances truly classified as earth, and not with plant-derived materials or ashes, while certain mineral earths remain permissible.
